newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola signs military pact with Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Angola signs military pact with Portugal.

text.p: Angola and its former coloniser Portugal signed a military cooperation agreement on Thursday to formalise existing military ties.

The agreement, which includes cooperation in training and technical assistance for the Angolan Armed Forces (FAA), was signed by Angolan Defence Minister Pedro Sebastiao and his Portuguese counterpart Antonia Vitorino in the capital Luanda.
"We have signed here an important legal instrument which will give effect to what we were already doing within the framework of general cooperation," Sebastiao told reporters at the ceremony.
Vitorino said the accord not only reinforced existing ties but also confirmed Portugal's commitment to the Angolan peace process.

"This is part of the creation of a single unified military. It has a part within the peace process and is a commitment by Portugal to support the project for the creation of a unified military," he said.

A single Angolan army including government soldiers and the former rebel UNITA movement is one of the key objectives of the 1994 Lusaka Protocol signed by both sides to end civil war which erupted on independence from Portugal in 1975.

Portugal is one of three observer countries in a joint ceasefire commission helping to implement the Lusaka accord. It has also sent several hundred soldiers to be part of the United Nations peace-keeping force in Angola.
Vitorino, who began his visit to Angola on Monday, returns home on Friday.
